AlternateTargets: come back to life after the end
Senses.Explanation: Literally, ‘after being completely cut off, revive again.’ The phrase occurs 222 times in 119 allowlisted texts. Its dominant fixed formula is ‘let go at the cliff and personally assent and undertake it; revive after being cut off, and you cannot deceive anyone’ (懸崖撒手，自肯承當；絕後再甦，欺君不得). Records also place it after ‘the life-root is severed’ (命根斷), beside ‘shed skin and exchange bones’ (去皮換骨), and compare it with a cold ember flaming and a withered tree flourishing again. One master explicitly departs from the inherited formula: ‘the former sages all wanted to revive after being cut off; I am not like that.’ The entry reports this recurrent sequence and its criticism without deciding what state the phrase denotes.
Senses.Note: Zen bends an ordinary death-and-revival image into a stock saying repeatedly quoted in teaching-seat discourse and biographies. It belongs with ‘let go at the cliff’ (懸崖撒手), ‘the life-root is severed’ (命根斷), and ‘gain life within death’ (死中得活), but remains one figurative referent rather than separate literal and technical objects.
